problemStatement.formal: For the nth prime p_n, the file assumes the PNT asymptotic and Dusart upper/lower bounds, then proves eventual (1\pm\epsilon)n\log n estimates, a subexponential PNT consequence, and a Dusart sandwich window.
problemStatement.plain: Backfill the nth-prime bound metadata around the Lean result: prime-index basics, PNT-derived eventual upper/lower bounds, Dusart upper and lower axioms, the sandwich interval for p_n, and the resulting asymptotic upper estimate.
whyMatters: Explicit nth-prime estimates are the numerical face of the prime number theorem.
The Lean file cleanly separates elementary consequences from the three analytic-number-theory axioms.
The metadata should show which parts are proven from the assumed PNT/Dusart facts and which facts remain imported assumptions.

proven: `nth_prime_is_prime` and `nth_prime_ge_two` provide the basic nth-prime interface.
`nth_prime_eventually_lt_mul` and `nth_prime_eventually_gt_mul` unpack the PNT asymptotic into eventual epsilon bounds.
`pnt_bound_subexponential`, `dusart_sandwich`, `dusart_gap_width`, and `dusart_upper_at_six` record concrete consequences of the analytic estimates.
`dusart_implies_asymptotic_upper` connects the explicit Dusart upper bound back to the asymptotic PNT-style ratio.
open: `nth_prime_asymptotic`, `dusart_upper_bound`, and `dusart_lower_bound` are axioms in `PrimeGapBoundsOQ01.lean`; the file has zero sorries.
knownResults.goal: Clarify that the formal work proves consequences of PNT/Dusart assumptions rather than deriving those analytic estimates from scratch.
